newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natural gas climbs on upcoming outage.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natural gas climbs on upcoming outage.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices continued their climb on Wednesday as players anticipated an outage next week on Alberta's pipeline network and strong western U.S. markets pushed up demand, traders said.

Spot gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was discussed at C$1.58 per gigajoule, up about three cents from Tuesday and over a dime from last week. August-October term gas was quoted at C$1.55 per gigajoule, on par with Tuesday.
The transportation charge to Empress was talked up slightly to a still-discounted 3-4 cents.

A Calgary-based trader said AECO's strength was being attributed to a maintenace outage on NOVA Gas Transmission's Grande Prairie mainline in northern Alberta slated to start Sunday, taking about one billion cubic feet per day of gas of the system.
The scheduled maintenace work was expected to run until late Thursday, a NOVA official said.
At Sumas, Wash., prices climbed again into the US$1.16/1.17 per million British thermal units range, up about 3 cents from Tuesday.

A trader of British Columbia gas said the jump was due to strong U.S. Rockies and San Juan markets, as well as heavy demand from California, where the 1,080 MW San Onofre nuclear unit was expect to remain off line until next week.
At Niagara, prices were pegged in the US$2.30 per mmmBtu range, up one or two cents from Tuesday. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
